content.prompt: Find, to the nearest minute, the angles of inclination of the tangents to the parabola $y=1-x^2$ at its $x$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=(1-x)(1+x)\\0&=(1-x)(1+x)\\x&=-1\text{ or }1\\f'(x)&=-2x\\f'(-1)&=-2(-1)=2\\f'(1)&=-2(1)=-2\end{aligned}$$
Use $\tan\theta=m$, with $0^\circ\leq\theta<180^\circ$.

At $(-1,0)$:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=2\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}(2)\\\theta&\approx63^\circ26'\end{aligned}$$
At $(1,0)$ the inclination is obtuse:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=-2\\\theta&=180^\circ-\tan^{-1}(2)\\\theta&\approx116^\circ34'\end{aligned}$$
